P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Yes. Serbian banks take deposits from individuals in dinars or foreign currency: Banca Intesa's general deposit terms define a deposit as money in dinars or in a foreign currency placed in a deposit account, with specific rules for individual (natural-person) clients, and require the bank to explain the risks when a service is in a foreign currency (Banca Intesa). Foreign-currency (devizni) accounts are standard; specific fees were not captured.

L2_tax_id.question: Tax ID: who needs one, how to get it?
L2_tax_id.answer: The PIB (poreski identifikacioni broj). Entrepreneurs (preduzetnici), legal entities and non-residents get a 9-digit PIB, usually through registration with the Business Registers Agency (APR). For resident individuals who are not entrepreneurs, the PIB is their 13-digit JMBG, the citizen's unique master number (Rulebook on the tax identification number). Taxpayers who do not register with the APR can apply for a PIB electronically on the Tax Administration's ePorezi portal (Biznis.rs, citing the Tax Administration).

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Flat 10%-20% by income type; lump-sum (pausal) regime for entrepreneurs not researched. Residents are generally taxed on worldwide income (see quoted rules). Work performed while living in Serbia for foreign clients is generally taxable there. Since 1 January 2023, unregistered freelancers paid from abroad self-assess quarterly (returns within 30 days after each quarter) and choose between two normative-expense models. One reduces quarterly gross income by a fixed RSD 96,000 per an updated source. Registered entrepreneurs can use the flat-rate (paušal) regime below about RSD 6 million turnover.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: The standard VAT rate is 20%. Mandatory VAT registration applies at RSD 8 million of total turnover in the previous 12 months, or expected turnover in the next year for new businesses. 2026 draft amendments to the VAT law do not raise it; a proposal to lift it to RSD 12 million has not been adopted. The paušal limit (RSD 6 million) is a separate test (see L7). Treatment of services to foreign clients was not captured.

L7_incentives.question: Legal incentives / tax holidays / special zones relevant to small digital businesses
L7_incentives.answer: Paušal (lump-sum) entrepreneur, the main regime for IT contractors: a fixed monthly payment of tax plus contributions, set by a Tax Administration decision based on the activity code and municipality, with bookkeeping reduced to an invoice register. The ceiling is RSD 6 million of revenue per calendar year (unchanged since 2013). A business opened mid-year gets the full RSD 6 million, not a pro-rated limit. Exceeding it ends paušal status and means switching to bookkeeping, but no extra tax on the excess. Existing bookkeeping entrepreneurs can apply to switch by the end of October for the next year. TRAP, the independence test: work for one permanent client is checked against nine dependency criteria (client's instructions and equipment, ban on other customers, etc.). Failing five or more reclassifies the income as 'other income', taxed at the payer's level (Art. 85(1)(17) ZPDG).

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (5) Client payments by PayPal (on PayPal's Payouts list as 'Send, receive, and withdraw'). (6) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
